newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: European diplomats, UN agencies hold Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: European diplomats, UN agencies hold Zaire talks.

text.p: European diplomats and officials from major humanitarian agencies began urgent talks in Geneva on Tuesday evening over the unfolding crisis in eastern Zaire, diplomats said.

The closed-door meeting, chaired by French Secretary of State for Emergency Humanitarian Action Xavier Emmanuelli, is to examine how the survival needs of an estimated 500,000 Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees in the Kivu area can be met.
It followed a warning issued in Brussels by the European Union's aid commissioner Emma Bonino that one million people -- many of them already refugees from Rwanda and Burundi -- could die in Zaire.
She accused the world of standing aloof from the tragedy.

Zairean troops and ethnic Tutsi rebels have been fighting a spreading war over the past 10 days, causing thousands of Burundian and Rwandan refugees to leave their camps and Zairean natives to leave their villages.
Zairean and Rwandan forces traded mortar and machinegun fire across their border on Tuesday in what aid officials said seemed to be the most serious exchange since one in late September.
The crisis talks were being held in the French diplomatic mission overlooking Lake Geneva, near the United Nations European headquarters in the Swiss city.
"The meeting has started. Mr. Emmanuelli is here," one diplomatic source at the French mission told Reuters.
No statements or press events were planned.

Belgian State Secretary for Cooperation and Development Reginald Moreels, whose office said he was travelling to Geneva on Tuesday evening for urgent talks with French and other officials on the situation in eastern Zaire, was expected soon.

Other representatives from European Union member states were attending, joined by officials from the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees and the U.N. World Food Programme.

It was not immediately clear whether any of the officials would contact Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, who is in Lausanne, Switzerland, receiving treatment for prostate cancer following an operation there two months ago.

Zaire's sick and absent president sought to reassert his authority in the east of his country by placing it under military rule and his interior minister accused Rwanda's Tutsi-led government of trying to carve out a Tutsi empire.

Reuters reporters and other witnesses in the Rwandan border town of Cyangugu, just across the border from Bukavu, on Tuesday spoke of exchanges lasting about two hours. Aid workers at one stage had to take refuge from the firing, they said.
Up to 400,000 Rwandan Hutus are currently cut off in the north of the Goma region and 300,000 are on the run in Uvira and Bukavu further south.
The Geneva-based UNHCR said on Tuesday it was trying to get hold of Western satellite pictures to trace hundreds of thousands of refugees fleeing the ethnic conflict in the east.

Augustine Mahiga, UNHCR's coordinator for the troubled region, said his agency had no access to up to 400,000 Rwandan Hutus cut off in north of Goma region because of fighting and 300,000 on the run in Uvira and Bukavu further south.
He told a news conference that UNHCR and aid agencies, which have pulled out of Bukavu and Uvira due to insecurity, had no way of knowing what the refugees were up to.
